description: Table 1, a single table rendered as an image, headed "Alloys" on the left and "Chemical compositions (at. %)" as a merged heading spanning four element columns labelled Fe, Mn, Al and Cu (in that left-to-right order). Three data rows follow: 15Al — Fe 44.6, Mn 35.2, Al 15.0, Cu 5.2; 17Al — Fe 43.2, Mn 34.8, Al 17.0, Cu 5.0; 19Al — Fe 41.6, Mn 34.8, Al 18.6, Cu 5.0. All values are in atomic percent and every cell is legible; there are no error bars, no additional columns and no carbon column. Read vertically, the table shows that as Al rises from 15.0 to 18.6 at.% the Fe content falls monotonically from 44.6 to 41.6 at.%, while Mn (35.2, 34.8, 34.8) and Cu (5.2, 5.0, 5.0) stay essentially constant — i.e. the nominal Al variations are achieved by substituting Al for Fe. The caption and the citing text state these compositions were measured by EDS, so the table's role is to fix the actual chemistry of the three Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density alloys whose hardness and aging behaviour the rest of the paper reports. No graphical panel accompanies this table.

observations.observation: The table's column header is 'Chemical compositions (at. %)' and spans exactly four element columns, labelled Fe, Mn, Al and Cu; there is no carbon column.
Row 15Al lists Fe 44.6, Mn 35.2, Al 15.0, Cu 5.2 at.%.
Row 17Al lists Fe 43.2, Mn 34.8, Al 17.0, Cu 5.0 at.%.
Row 19Al lists Fe 41.6, Mn 34.8, Al 18.6, Cu 5.0 at.%.
Fe content decreases monotonically with increasing Al: 44.6 at.% (15Al) > 43.2 at.% (17Al) > 41.6 at.% (19Al), while Mn (35.2, 34.8, 34.8) and Cu (5.2, 5.0, 5.0) are essentially constant.
The alloy label '19Al' corresponds to a measured Al content of 18.6 at.%, i.e. slightly below the nominal 19 at.%.
The caption states that Table 1 gives the chemical compositions of the 15Al, 17Al and 19Al alloys.
The citing text states the alloys have nominal compositions Fe-35Mn-xAl-5Cu (at.%, x = 15, 17, 19) and are referred to as 15Al, 17Al and 19Al according to their Al contents.
The citing text states the compositions in Table 1 were measured via Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy (EDS); the table image itself contains no EDS annotation.
The citing text states the ingots were produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under argon.
The citing text states the densities of 15Al, 17Al and 19Al were measured by the Archimedes method as 6.85, 6.76 and 6.66 g·cm-3; these values are not present in the table image.

subfigures.description: Two-level-header table: row labels 15Al, 17Al, 19Al versus columns Fe, Mn, Al, Cu under the merged heading 'Chemical compositions (at. %)'. Values 44.6/35.2/15.0/5.2 (15Al), 43.2/34.8/17.0/5.0 (17Al) and 41.6/34.8/18.6/5.0 (19Al). All cells legible.
